name: Baby Bottle
description: A baby with a bottle means an actual infant is in the picture: feeding time, a new-parent status, or a careful hint about a pregnancy. It is not a joke about an adult being babyish.
meaning: The baby is the person and the bottle is the feeding, the gear, or the clue that a baby is coming. 👶🍼 is literal. Used to mock a grown person, the bottle makes the insult look like you are talking about a real child.
examples: we are going to need these 👶🍼
seoDescription: What does 👶🍼 mean? A real baby: feeding time, new-parent life, or a careful pregnancy hint. It is not an insult for adults.

longForm.overview:
The baby emoji is how people coo at something small and new, and the bottle emoji is more specific still. It means bottles, feeding, and often the soft announcement that a household is about to include an infant. 👶🍼 is the status new parents send at 3 a.m., the photo caption of a tiny person and a burp cloth, and the hint friends send only when they are sure the news is theirs to hint. "We are going to need these" is a pregnancy or adoption tell. Read it as big news if the sender is allowed to be telling you. Read it as ordinary chaos if they already have the baby and the message is about sleep.

It is a bad joke about an adult. Calling a coworker 👶🍼 because they needed help does two kinds of damage: it infantilizes them, and it looks, in the scrollback, like you announced a baby. The bottle is that literal. Also be careful around fertility. A playful "your turn 👶🍼" aimed at someone who has not asked for that conversation is not playful. You do not know who is trying, who is grieving a loss, or who is done. Wait to be invited. When the news is real and welcome, the pair is a warm reaction to an announcement, better with the parent's name and the baby's name if you have it. Cooing without listening is how people miss the request for a meal or a nap.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👶🍼 marks feeding logs in family chats, "we are alive" updates, and registry hints. Grandparents send it when they are on duty. Friends send it when they are dropping off food and do not expect the parents to answer.

The announcement version is rarer and more charged. If you are not sure the news is public, do not screenshot it. A bottle in a private thread may be a secret for another week.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 👶🍼 to tease an adult, a couple without children, or anyone whose reproductive life you do not share. The emoji cannot tell who is hurting.

Do not send it as a demand for baby pictures. Parents will share when they want. And do not use it in a work channel as a joke about a project being "the baby." Someone will congratulate a pregnancy that does not exist.
longForm.howToReply:
On a feeding update, a short kindness is enough. Do not ask for a recap of the night if they are clearly trying to sleep between bottles.

On a hint about expecting, follow their lead. If they told you plainly, congratulations and "what do you need" are the grown-up reply. If you are unsure, do not blast the group. Ask them privately what they are comfortable saying. Excitement can wait five minutes for consent.

faqs.question: What does 👶🍼 mean?
faqs.answer: 👶🍼 means a real baby is being fed, announced, or prepared for. The baby is the person. The bottle is feeding, gear, or the clue that a baby is on the way.

faqs.question: Is 👶🍼 a pregnancy announcement?
faqs.answer: It can be, in a phrase like "we will need these." If they already have an infant, it is usually a feeding update. Do not spread either version without checking.

faqs.question: Can I send 👶🍼 as a joke about my friend?
faqs.answer: Skip it. It reads as a literal baby, and as an insult about an adult it is meaner than the joke feels when you type it.

faqs.question: How do I reply to a 3 a.m. 👶🍼?
faqs.answer: You often do not need to, until morning. If you reply, keep it short. They may be feeding with one hand.

conversationExamples.interpretation: A parent is up with an infant. Do not start a long thread. Offer help only if you are actually nearby and awake.

conversationExamples.message: telling you first, we are in 👶🍼 season
conversationExamples.interpretation: A private announcement. Congratulate them and ask what they want kept quiet. Do not post it.

conversationExamples.message: my sister had the baby, I am on 👶🍼 support this week
conversationExamples.interpretation: Their week got claimed by family. Be flexible about plans. The baby is not a metaphor for the relationship.
A scheduling fact and personal news. Congratulate them and sort coverage. The bottle is not a joke about the handoff.

conversationExamples.message: photo dump is mostly 👶🍼 ignore if you are not in the mood
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are sharing baby photos with an opt-out. You can react warmly or scroll. They gave you permission to skip.
